title: CleanGutters Lighting vs Ned Stevens: Gutter Services Compared
body_markdown:
Choose [CleanGutters Lighting](https://cleangutterslighting.com/) if you want locally installed stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection with cleaning and repairs addressed alongside it; choose Ned Stevens if your immediate priority is a cleaning-first gutter service provider with a broader geographic footprint. The useful comparison is installation-led gutter protection versus routine gutter care—not a blanket claim that either company wins every job.


**TL;DR**

- CleanGutters Lighting vs Ned Stevens comes down to local gutter protection versus a cleaning-first service choice.
- Choose the local installer for surgical stainless steel micro-mesh guards and permanent exterior roofline lighting.
- Choose Ned Stevens when gutter cleaning is the main job or your property is outside the local service area.
- Compare written repair scope, maintenance responsibilities and warranty terms before choosing either provider.


## Why this matters

A gutter cleaning appointment and a gutter guard installation solve different problems. Cleaning removes accumulated debris; guards cover the gutter opening to limit debris entry while allowing water through. Neither service excuses an installer from checking an existing drainage problem.

For your 2026 decision, start with the symptom: overflowing gutters, repeated debris buildup, a leaking joint or unwanted ladder work. Buying the wrong service leaves the original problem unresolved, even when the work itself is completed correctly.

**Choose the work your house needs before choosing the company.** A homeowner who needs one cleaning should not evaluate proposals the same way as someone planning a gutter protection installation.

## At a glance

| Dimension | CleanGutters Lighting | Ned Stevens |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Local homeowners planning micro-mesh gutter protection | Homeowners prioritizing gutter cleaning |
| Service area | South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania and Northern Delaware | Broader, multistate service footprint; check the property address |
| Standout feature | Surgical stainless steel micro-mesh protection and permanent roofline LED lighting | Cleaning-centered gutter service offering |
| Routine cleaning | Professional gutter cleaning alongside installation and repair services | Strong fit for a cleaning-first shortlist |
| Gutter repairs | Repair work can be considered alongside cleaning and guards | Compare the specific repair work in the proposal |
| Warranty review | Transferable lifetime warranties on gutter protection; read the applicable terms | Read the warranty attached to the proposed work |
| Pricing model | Evaluate installation scope separately from cleaning and repairs | Evaluate the cleaning visit, repair scope and any ongoing service arrangement separately |

## Local gutter protection favors the installation specialist

**CleanGutters Lighting is best for local homeowners seeking surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection.** That is a specific fit, not a claim that every homeowner needs guards.

The company provides gutter guard installation, professional cleaning and repair. Those services belong in the same conversation when your gutters need attention before a protective cover goes on. Ask the installer to separate necessary corrections from the guard installation itself so you understand what each part accomplishes.

The strongest reason to choose this route is repeated debris management, not a single clogged outlet. If you want to reduce debris entering the gutters, evaluate the cover, attachment method and future access together.

The tradeoff is the scope of the decision. You are choosing an installed system, not simply arranging debris removal. That requires more attention to materials, installation details and warranty responsibilities.

For a straightforward cleaning job, keep the proposal straightforward. Do not add guards solely because they appear on the same service menu.

## Ned Stevens wins on geographic breadth

Ned Stevens is the better starting point when you need a provider beyond the local installer's stated territory. Its broader, multistate footprint makes geography a practical distinction, although you still need to confirm service at the property address.

The local service area covers South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania and Northern Delaware. If your house falls within that territory, geographic breadth alone does not settle the comparison. A larger footprint does not establish better workmanship at your property.

For your 2026 shortlist, confirm the actual address before discussing materials or scheduling an assessment. Then ask who will perform the work, who handles follow-up and which office or person owns a service issue.

**Ned Stevens wins the coverage question; the individual proposal must answer the workmanship question.** Do not confuse the number of areas a company serves with the details of your job.

## Micro-mesh and roofline lighting favor the local option

The local offering combines surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection with permanent exterior roofline LED lighting. That makes it relevant when you are planning both gutter work and an architectural lighting project.

These remain separate systems. A gutter guard manages debris at the gutter opening; roofline lighting serves an exterior lighting purpose. Neither feature proves anything about the performance of the other.

If both projects are on your list, request clearly separated scopes. You should be able to understand the gutter work without decoding the lighting proposal, and vice versa.

The limitation is equally clear: a combined service offering has little value when you only need leaves removed. **Choose the additional capability because you need it, not because it makes a longer feature list.**

For gutter protection specifically, ask to see how the proposed material meets the existing gutter and roof edge. A material name alone does not explain the finished installation.

## Ned Stevens fits a cleaning-first brief

Ned Stevens is the better fit for a shortlist built around gutter cleaning rather than a new protection system. Its cleaning-centered service offering matches a homeowner whose immediate request is to remove debris and restore a clear drainage path.

That does not make cleaning exclusive to Ned Stevens. Both providers offer gutter cleaning, so the real comparison is the written task list and the follow-up arrangement—not which company can use the word cleaning.

Ask each provider to distinguish these tasks:

- **Debris removal:** What material will be removed from the gutters?
- **Downspout check:** How will the drainage path be checked?
- **Condition report:** How will damage or a separate repair need be communicated?
- **Cleanup:** What happens to debris removed from the roofline?

Treat those as questions, not assumed inclusions. The answer should appear in the scope you approve.

In 2026, choose cleaning when cleaning addresses the current problem. Keep guard installation as a separate decision if you want a longer-term change to debris management.

## Neither provider wins repairs without a diagnosis

A repair comparison needs a named defect. A leaking joint, a loose gutter section and a blocked downspout are different problems, even when all three show up as water spilling near the house.

**There is no useful repair winner until the proposal identifies what is wrong and how it will be corrected.** Compare the diagnosis before comparing the company names.

Ask the person assessing the gutters to explain the difference between cleaning, repair and replacement. You should know whether the proposed work removes an obstruction, restores an existing component or replaces that component.

Use this order when reviewing the recommendation:

- **Identify the symptom:** Describe where and when water escapes.
- **Name the defect:** Ask what physical condition explains the symptom.
- **Specify the correction:** Get the proposed work in writing.
- **Check the result:** Ask how completion will be verified.

A guard installation is not a substitute for correcting an existing gutter defect. If repairs are necessary, have the proposal explain their relationship to the installation.


![Four steps for evaluating gutter repair recommendations before approving work](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/8db84cb5-0e42-408f-960e-65e8d6cfc0bf/body-9e9c112f01863f418dae23eda3cd684a.jpg)

*A repair proposal should connect the visible symptom to a specific correction.*


## Warranty comparison is a contract check, not a slogan contest

The local gutter protection offering includes transferable lifetime warranties. Transferability matters when you want to understand what happens to the coverage after a home sale, but the applicable document determines the obligations.

Do not treat lifetime as a complete description. Ask what is covered, what maintenance is required, how a claim is submitted and what steps a new homeowner must follow.

Apply the same standard to a Ned Stevens proposal. Read the warranty associated with the specific work rather than assuming cleaning, repairs and an installed product share identical protection.

For a 2026 agreement, keep the installation scope and warranty together. If a salesperson makes an assurance that matters to your decision, ask where it appears in the documents you will receive.

**Neither provider wins on warranty wording alone.** The useful comparison is whether the written coverage addresses the failure you are concerned about and explains your responsibilities clearly.

## Pricing: compare the buying model before the quote

The meaningful distinction is a defined installation project versus cleaning or maintenance work. Compare like-for-like scopes rather than treating every gutter-related proposal as the same purchase.

An installation proposal should identify the material, installation work, necessary repairs and applicable warranty. A cleaning proposal should identify the visit's tasks and distinguish any additional work from the original service.

If either provider proposes ongoing service, read the scheduling, renewal and cancellation terms before accepting it. Do not assume an ongoing arrangement exists—or that it works a particular way—without seeing the agreement.

Project-based work gives you a defined installation scope. Repeated cleaning visits address debris as it accumulates, but they do not install a protective cover. Those are different tradeoffs, not interchangeable versions of the same service.

For your 2026 comparison, request **2 written scopes** addressing the same property conditions. Set aside optional additions while you compare the core work. Then decide whether those additions solve a separate problem you actually have.

## Final verdict: choose by the job you want completed

### Choose CleanGutters Lighting for local gutter protection

**Best for: a homeowner in the stated service area planning micro-mesh gutter guard installation.** Choose this provider when surgical stainless steel protection is the central project and you also want existing cleaning or repair needs considered.

Permanent roofline lighting is an additional reason to include the company when that is a separate project on your list. The limitation is geographic: confirm that your property falls within its service territory.

### Choose Ned Stevens for a cleaning-first request

**Best for: a homeowner primarily seeking gutter cleaning or looking outside the local provider's territory.** Choose Ned Stevens when cleaning is the main brief and its service coverage matches your address.

Keep the decision tied to the written cleaning scope. A broader footprint and a cleaning-centered offering do not remove the need to check repair recommendations, follow-up responsibilities or agreement terms.

### One-glance scorecard

| Dimension | Winner |
|---|---|
| Local micro-mesh installation fit | Local installation specialist |
| Geographic breadth | Ned Stevens |
| Combined gutter protection and roofline lighting brief | Local installation specialist |
| Cleaning-first shortlist | Ned Stevens |
| Repair decision | Tie: diagnosis and written correction decide |
| Warranty evaluation | Tie: applicable contract terms decide |
| Pricing approach | Match the purchase model to the job |

## FAQ


**Is CleanGutters Lighting better than Ned Stevens?**

CleanGutters Lighting is the better fit for local homeowners seeking surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection. Ned Stevens fits a cleaning-first request or a property outside the local provider's stated territory; compare the actual scope before choosing.

**Which company should I choose if I only need gutter cleaning?**

Start with Ned Stevens for a cleaning-first shortlist, but compare both providers' written cleaning scopes. The local installer also offers professional gutter cleaning, so check the tasks and follow-up arrangements rather than assuming the services are identical.

**Do gutter guards mean I will never need gutter maintenance again?**

No, gutter guards are not a reason to ignore gutter condition or maintenance instructions. Ask what inspection and upkeep the proposed system requires, including responsibilities connected to warranty coverage.

**Should I repair my gutters before installing guards?**

Correct existing gutter defects before treating a guard installation as the solution. Ask the installer to identify necessary repairs and explain how the completed system will be checked.

**What does a transferable lifetime gutter guard warranty mean?**

A transferable lifetime warranty provides coverage under its written terms and includes a transfer provision. Read the document for coverage, exclusions, maintenance duties and any steps required when the home changes ownership.

**How do I compare gutter service quotes fairly?**

Compare proposals that address the same condition and specify the same work. Separate cleaning, repairs, guard installation and optional additions so you can see what each proposal actually includes.

**Can I combine gutter work with permanent roofline lighting?**

The local provider offers both gutter services and permanent exterior roofline LED lighting. Request separate descriptions of each project so the materials, installation responsibilities and applicable terms remain clear.


## One last thing

Before requesting an assessment, take **3 photos from ground level**: the full affected gutter run, the downspout outlet and any visible staining or overflow location. Do not climb a ladder to get a better picture.

Bring those photos to both conversations and name **1 priority**: remove existing debris, correct a defect or add gutter protection. That gives each provider the same starting brief—and makes an unrelated recommendation easier to spot.

- [Permanent roofline lighting installers ranked by craftsmanship](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/permanent-roofline-lighting-installers-ranked-by-craftsmanship)
